blocking.section: Decision outcome (Consensus row, Figure 2), Consequences, Confirmation (Fencing test)
blocking.issue: The fencing argument confuses Raft commit with state-machine acceptance, so the safety claim is false and the Confirmation test cannot be built as written. In hashicorp/raft every entry that reaches a voter quorum commits. The FSM only decides whether to accept it, and `ApplyFuture.Response()` returns that verdict. A deposed leader's entry can also commit later. Example: leader L1 proposes assignment A at sequence n+1, replicates it to follower F, then is partitioned. F wins the election with A in its log and signs its own assignment B at n+1. A precedes B in the log, so A commits and applies and B is rejected, although B is also committed. Two consequences follow. (1) 'replicas serve Nodes only committed entries' would let a replica deliver B, which carries a valid leader signature at (storeEpoch, n+1). The Node-side highest-pair check cannot tell A from B, so two Nodes could activate different assignments at the same sequence. Only state the FSM accepted may be served. (2) A new leader that signs its next sequence before its FSM has applied the entries from earlier terms is rejected on every proposal. The design needs the leader services to start after `raft.Barrier()` on election, and it needs a rule that a proposal whose FSM response is a rejection is re-read and re-signed. Figure 2 also shows the FSM applying before the quorum commit, which is the reverse of Raft's order. The owning document's 'so a deposed leader cannot commit' has the same imprecision, so the ADR should state the rule precisely and propose the amendment.
blocking.evidence: Consensus row: "The state machine applies an assignment or promotion only at the current sequence plus one; replicas serve Nodes only committed entries" / Consequences: "Good, because the apply-time sequence check fences a deposed leader: its stale-sequence entry never commits, so no replica delivers it." / Figure 2: "R->>R: apply only if the sequence is current plus one" followed by "R-->>S: committed on a voter quorum" / Confirmation: "**Fencing test**, Planned (M2): a deposed leader's proposal at a stale sequence never commits"
blocking.fix: Consensus row: replace the clause with "replicas serve Nodes only assignments and promotions the state machine accepted, never a committed entry it rejected; leader services start only after `raft.Barrier()` on election, and a rejected proposal is re-read and re-signed at the next sequence". Consequence: "Good, because the apply-time sequence check fences a deposed leader: of two signed entries at one sequence only the first in log order is accepted, and no replica delivers the other." Figure 2: put "R-->>R: committed on a voter quorum" before "R->>R: accept only if the sequence is current plus one", then "R-->>S: accepted assignment". Confirmation: "a deposed leader's entry at a sequence already taken is committed but never accepted or delivered, and a new leader proposes only after Barrier". Add a Proposed amendments item asking Control plane and GitOps to reword 'cannot commit' as 'cannot have a stale-sequence entry accepted'. The body is at 1,481 of 1,500 words, so shorten the existing clauses rather than append.

blocking.section: Decision outcome (Transport and Membership rows, Figure 1)
blocking.issue: Port 8092 cannot work as described. `raft.NewNetworkTransport` owns its `StreamLayer`: it calls `Accept()` in a loop and decodes every accepted connection as a Raft RPC. Figure 1 also sends content replication through the same 'Mutual-TLS stream layer on 8092', and the owning document adds write forwarding, status forwarding, the relay feed and a token `Join` on that port. Unless a demultiplexer sits in front of NetworkTransport, non-Raft traffic reaches the Raft decoder. The Transport row also admits 'Ruralz Control peer certificates only'. The Membership row says `ruralz control join` adds a voter over 8092, but a joining replica has no peer certificate yet: the owning document says it 'redeems a one-time `admin` token in `Join`, and the leader signs the replica's certificate'. With the client-certificate requirement the Transport row implies, the TLS handshake for `Join` fails, so the ADR contradicts itself and its owning document. The relay role certificate, Planned (M4), also needs class limits that 'peer certificates only' does not express.
blocking.evidence: Transport row: "`raft.NetworkTransport` over a Ruralz mutual-TLS stream layer on `crypto/tls`, never the built-in TCP layer, on 8092 ...; Ruralz Control peer certificates only, Node certificates rejected (TB-11)" / Membership row: "`ruralz control join` adds a voter over 8092" / Figure 1: "cas --> tls" and "tls -.->|\"Raft and content replication\"| peers" / owning document, Replica roles 4: "8092 authorizes classes by certificate role ... and a token `Join` (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-15)"
blocking.fix: Rewrite the Transport row: "A Ruralz mutual-TLS stream layer on `crypto/tls` listens on 8092 and names each connection's class, proposed by ALPN (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-15). It hands only Raft-class connections from voter peer certificates to `raft.NetworkTransport` through its `Accept`, and gives the other classes their own connections. Only `Join` accepts a one-time token without a client certificate (`VerifyClientCertIfGiven`). Node certificates are always rejected (TB-11)." In Figure 1, label the edge "Raft, content and forwarding classes". Remove the now-redundant ALPN clause from the Proposed amendments bullet to stay within 1,500 words.

blocking.issue: The main reason given for the choice contradicts the ADR's own Pros and cons and the research. Dragonboat also ships consensus, a built-in transport, Pebble log storage and built-in snapshotting and log compaction, so hashicorp/raft is not 'the only researched library' that ships these together. What actually separates them is S1: dragonboat has had no release since 2023 and its master is unstable. As written, the reader can refute the decision from the ADR's own dragonboat section.
blocking.evidence: Decision outcome: "because it is the only researched library that ships consensus, a pure-Go log store, a network transport and a file snapshot store together" / Pros and cons, dragonboat: "Good, because it is Apache-2.0 with built-in transport, snapshotting and log compaction" / research go-libraries-runtime.md section 6: dragonboat Transport "Built in, pluggable", Log storage "Pebble by default", Snapshots "Built-in snapshotting and log compaction"
blocking.fix: Replace with: "because, of the researched libraries with a release in the last 12 months (S1), it is the only one that ships consensus, a pure-Go log store, a network transport and a file snapshot store together (sources as now); it released v1.8.0 on 2026-09-16; ...". The word count stays about the same.

non_blocking.suggestion: hashicorp/raft reports commit time, FSM apply time, leader changes and snapshot metrics through the global hashicorp/go-metrics registry, and the default sink discards them. Only the hclog-to-slog adapter is decided. Add that a Ruralz go-metrics `MetricSink` forwards them to OpenTelemetry for `/metrics` on 9902, so quorum loss and leader churn get the degraded-state metric P10 requires. It must not use go-metrics' Prometheus or Circonus sink packages, because the Circonus sink would link the MPL-2.0 go-cleanhttp and fail the license gate, and the `/metrics` exporter is unselected (OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-16).

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (Content store row) and owning document per-peer cap
non_blocking.suggestion: Say that Raft traffic never shares a connection, or the 64 MiB/s per-peer budget, with content replication. Otherwise a large Revision fetch can delay AppendEntries heartbeats past the 1000 ms timeout and cause needless elections.

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (Content store and Snapshots rows)
non_blocking.suggestion: State that a replica serves an assignment only once its referenced content objects are local and verified. This matters after `InstallSnapshot` or a join, when the FSM references digests the replica has not fetched yet. Also state that deletion of unreferenced Revisions, beyond the latest 50, is itself a Raft entry, so a backup 'consistent at one index' never finds content missing.

v1.8.0 persists the commit index only when the LogStore implements raft's commit-tracking interface. The research says raft-boltdb/v2 v2.4.2 is the 'matching release' but does not confirm it implements that interface. Qualify the claim, for example 'when the log store supports it', or have the Planned (M2) integration test confirm it.

The PostgreSQL con relies on single-host Raft installs. The Membership row lists only three or five voters. Say that one voter is allowed for single-host and development installs, with no failure tolerance, so the self-contained-install driver also covers one replica.

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (Log and stable store row)
non_blocking.suggestion: bbolt files do not shrink after raft-boltdb truncates the log, and Consul operators report this. Name a bound, or say that `ruralz control backup` then `restore` compacts the file, and record the growth as a Bad consequence.
